## 0. Conventions, hypotheses, and inputs

Throughout k has characteristic zero and B is a locally Noetherian k-scheme. Notation is as in the theorem statement. Since char(k)=0 the normalised trace (1/4)tr splits the unit O_P -> gamma_*O_C, so gamma_*O_C = O_P (+) E^vee with E locally free of rank three; this is the packet's Tschirnhausen bundle. From chi(O_{C_b}) = 1-6 = -5 = chi(O_{P^1}) + chi(E_b^vee) = 1 + (deg E_b^vee + 3) we get deg E_b = 9 on every geometric fibre.

The projective-bundle convention is fixed by p_*O_X(1) = E, hence p_*O_X(2) = Sym^2 E. This is the packet convention: with E = O(3)^3 and F = O(4)(+)O(5) one gets h^0(P^1, Sym^2 E (x) F^vee) = 6*3 + 6*2 = 30, matching the rank count 26+4 = 30 recorded independently in REV-0109's check of CLM-0065-6.

**Verified dependency artifacts used.** ATT-0065 (subproblem C66-GEO-Z), confirmed independently by REV-0108 (pass 1) and REV-0109 (pass 2), every claim CLM-0065-1 ... CLM-0065-9 with verdict `confirmed`. I use exactly:
- CLM-0065-1: pi_*W and pi_*(W|_Gamma) locally free of ranks 26 and 12 with arbitrary base change, Fit_0(coker phi) = I_12(phi);
- CLM-0065-3: the filtered snake reduction coker(phi) = coker(phi_5) with no global splitting;
- CLM-0065-4: **Fit_0(coker phi) = a_N^*I_e**, commuting with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change, with the T-point criterion "N_T = pi_T^*M_T for an invertible M_T on T";
- CLM-0065-5: the canonical filtration 0 -> W_4 -> W -> W_5 -> 0 from the sub-line-bundle O_P(5) (x) s^*s_*F(-5) of F, of relative degrees 20 and 16;
- CLM-0065-6: the exact sequence 0 -> End(F) -> p_*scriptW -> gamma_*W -> 0 on P;
- CLM-0065-8: R^1 s_*End(F) = 0 under (H-BAL);
- CLM-0065-7, CLM-0065-9: the ambient/intrinsic comparison under the two ambient hypotheses.

ATT-0065's hypotheses are met verbatim over the base Conf := Conf_6(C/B): Conf is locally Noetherian and of finite type over B, C_Conf -> Conf is smooth proper with genus-6 geometric fibres, the six tautological sections are pairwise disjoint by construction, and d_4 - n = 20-6 = 14 > 2g-2 = 10 while d_5 - n = 16-6 = 10 = 2g-2. So Fit_0(coker phi) = a_N^*I_e holds on Conf.

**Established working-context facts used (used directly, as permitted).**
- (WC-112) A hyperelliptic genus-six degree-four cover has E = O(1)(+)O(4)(+)O(4) and cannot have balanced F = O(4)(+)O(5). (Cross-checked by packet FND-0125, which sharpens it to F = O(2)(+)O(7).)
- (WC-118) When h^0(L)=3, p is a base point of |L| exactly when h^0(O_C(D+p))=3; for a smooth plane quintic with omega = 2H and D = H-p one has L = H+p.
- The CE degree formula deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12-4f and deg(O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_C) = 2g-2+8 = 18 at g=6 (source SRC-0004, packet primary locator).

**Source-backed input, not proved here.** (H-CE), the degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl structure theorem, is assumed exactly as ATT-0065 assumes it. A literature check confirms the standard normalisation deg E = deg F = g+3 = 9 for degree-four covers of P^1, consistent with the deg E = 9 computed above and with (H-BAL).

**Computational hypothesis, explicitly non-load-bearing.** Non-vacuity of (H-BAL) is supported by the pinned reusable computation of the (1,2)-(2,2) complete intersection in P^1 x P^2 with E^vee = O(-3)^3 and F = O(4)(+)O(5) [sha256 823546d61b9bfb1863be8693a9d2c5fe53bdee4736e3e4090ebccdb633621eec]. A finite computation cannot establish a universal claim; the theorem below is a conditional statement about balanced families and no step of its proof uses that example.

## 1. det F versus det E, and the relative canonical normalisation (part A)

**Lemma 1.1.** Let N be an invertible sheaf on P = P^1_B whose restriction to every geometric fibre of s has degree 0. Then R^1 s_*N = 0, s_*N is invertible and commutes with arbitrary base change, and the counit s^*s_*N -> N is an isomorphism.

*Proof.* R^1 s_* is the top pushforward for the relative curve s, so it commutes with arbitrary base change; its geometric fibres are H^1(P^1, O) = 0, so R^1 s_*N = 0 by Nakayama. Locally Rs_*N is a perfect complex [E^0 -> E^1] of amplitude [0,1] with H^1 = 0; the map is then surjective onto a free module, hence split, so its kernel s_*N is a direct summand of E^0, hence locally free, and the splitting is preserved by any base change, so s_*N commutes with arbitrary base change. Its rank is h^0(P^1,O) = 1. The counit s^*s_*N -> N is a map of invertible sheaves which on each geometric fibre is the evaluation of a nonzero section of O_{P^1}, hence an isomorphism there; a fibrewise surjective map of invertible sheaves is surjective by Nakayama, and a surjection of invertible sheaves is an isomorphism. []

Note that Lemma 1.1 uses no reducedness of B and no constant-fibre-rank argument for a lower pushforward; this is the discipline demanded by packet FND-0131.

By (H-BAL), deg F_b = 4+5 = 9 = deg E_b, so det F (x) det E^vee has fibrewise degree 0 and Lemma 1.1 gives a unique invertible A on B with

  det F = det E (x) s^*A.  (1.1)

Because C is the zero scheme of a regular section of the rank-two bundle scriptW (that is the content of the Koszul shape of (H-CE): the resolution is the Koszul complex 0 -> Lambda^2 scriptW^vee -> scriptW^vee -> I_C -> 0, using Lambda^2 scriptW^vee = O_X(-4) (x) p^*det F), the conormal sheaf is N_{C/X} = scriptW|_C = W and adjunction gives

  omega_{C/P} = omega_{X/P}|_C (x) det W.

With the convention p_*O_X(1) = E the relative Euler sequence is 0 -> Omega_{X/P}(1) -> p^*E -> O_X(1) -> 0, whence p^*det E = omega_{X/P} (x) O_X(3), i.e. omega_{X/P} = O_X(-3) (x) p^*det E. Also det W = (O_X(4) (x) p^*det F^vee)|_C. Therefore

  omega_{C/P} = O_X(1)|_C (x) gamma^*(det E (x) det F^vee) = O_X(1)|_C (x) pi^*A^{-1}.  (1.2)

Equivalently O_X(1)|_C = omega_{C/P} (x) pi^*A = omega_{C/B} (x) gamma^*O_P(2) (x) pi^*A, using omega_{C/P} = omega_{C/B} (x) gamma^*omega_{P/B}^{-1} and omega_{P/B} = O_P(-2).

Arithmetic check: fibrewise deg(det E (x) det F^vee) = 0, so deg(omega_{C/P}) = deg(O_X(1)|_C) = 18, matching both SRC-0004's 2g-2+4*2 = 18 and the direct value 2g-2 + 2*4 = 18. The two independent computations agree.

By CLM-0065-5 the filtration sub-line-bundle of F is L_5 = O_P(5) (x) s^*Lambda with Lambda := s_*F(-5) invertible on B, so W_5 = i^*(O_X(2) (x) p^*L_5^vee) = O_X(2)|_C (x) gamma^*O_P(-5) (x) pi^*Lambda^{-1}. Substituting (1.2),

  W_5 = omega_{C/B}^{(x)2} (x) gamma^*O_P(-1) (x) pi^*T = omega_{C/B}^{(x)2}(-D) (x) pi^*T,
  L  = W_5 (x) omega_{C/B}^{-1} = omega_{C/B}(-D) (x) pi^*T,  T := A^{(x)2} (x) Lambda^{-1}.  (1.3)

This proves (A). Two remarks. First, this *derives* the relative-canonical normalisation listed on the frontier as an external assumption ("(N) remains an external assumption"), from (H-CE) alone; it does not restate the packet's weak form. Packet FND-0105 anticipated that the residual freedom is pinned by degree; here the residual freedom is pinned instead by Lemma 1.1, which also yields the correct relative statement (a twist by pi^* of an invertible sheaf on B, not literal triviality). Second, **all later statements are insensitive to that twist**: relative triviality in Pic^0 is triviality modulo pi^*Pic(B); pi_*(L (x) pi^*T) = (pi_*L) (x) T so P_B(pi_*L) is unchanged; and |L_b| is unchanged fibrewise. I will use this without further comment.

Degrees: deg L = 10-4 = 6 and deg W_5 = 20-4 = 16, agreeing with the packet degree formula.

## 2. The Maroni formula for h^0(L) and h^1(L) (part B)

For the finite flat gamma, relative duality gives gamma_*omega_{C/P} = Hom_{O_P}(gamma_*O_C, O_P) = (gamma_*O_C)^vee, so

  gamma_*omega_{C/B} = (gamma_*O_C)^vee (x) omega_{P/B} = (O_P (+) E)(-2).  (2.1)

By (1.3) and the projection formula,

  gamma_*L = gamma_*(omega_{C/B}) (x) O_P(-1) (x) s^*T = (O_P(-3) (+) E(-3)) (x) s^*T.  (2.2)

Since gamma is finite, R^i pi_* = R^i s_* o gamma_*. On a geometric fibre with E_b = (+)_i O(a_i), sum a_i = 9,

  h^0(L_b) = h^0(O(-3)) + sum_i h^0(O(a_i-3)) = sum_i max(0, a_i-2),
  h^1(L_b) = h^1(O(-3)) + sum_i h^1(O(a_i-3)) = 2 + sum_i max(0, 2-a_i).  (2.3)

Consistency: h^0-h^1 = sum_i (a_i-2) - 2 = 9-6-2 = 1 = chi(L_b), as required by Riemann-Roch for deg L = 6, g = 6. Dually h^0(O_{C_b}(D_b)) = h^0(P^1, O(1) (x) gamma_*O_C) = h^0(O(1)) + sum_i h^0(O(1-a_i)) = 2 + sum_i max(0,2-a_i) = h^1(L_b), which is Serre duality h^1(L) = h^0(omega (x) L^{-1}) = h^0(O(D)). Hence

  h^0(L_b) = 3  <=>  min_i a_i >= 2  <=>  h^0(O(D_b)) = 2  <=>  h^1(L_b) = 2.  (2.4)

This answers, in closed form and stratum by stratum, the frontier question "which values of h^0(L) occur": h^0(L) is the Maroni-type invariant sum_i max(0,a_i-2). For instance (3,3,3), (2,3,4), (2,2,5) all give h^0(L)=3, while (1,4,4) gives 4. Clifford (Step 3) forbids min a_i = 0.

## 3. (H-BAL) forces min a_i >= 2, and unconditional base change (part C)

Fix a geometric point b. By (1.3) and Riemann-Roch, chi(L_b)=1, so h^0(L_b) >= 1, i.e. h^1(O(D_b)) = h^0(omega(-D_b)) = h^0(L_b) >= 1 and D_b is special. Clifford's theorem gives h^0(O(D_b)) - 1 <= deg(D_b)/2 = 2, so h^0(O(D_b)) <= 3. In the equality case h^0(O(D_b))=3, since deg D_b = 4 is neither 0 nor 2g-2 = 10, Clifford's equality clause forces C_b hyperelliptic with D_b linearly equivalent to twice the hyperelliptic class H_2. Then h_*O_{C_b} = O (+) O(-7) (from chi), so H^0(O(2H_2)) = h^*H^0(O_{P^1}(2)) is three-dimensional and consists entirely of pullbacks; hence the base-point-free pencil defining gamma_b is h^* of a pencil of degree-two divisors on P^1 and gamma_b = q o h factors through the hyperelliptic map. By (WC-112) such a cover has E = O(1)(+)O(4)(+)O(4) and F not isomorphic to O(4)(+)O(5), contradicting (H-BAL). (Packet FND-0125 records the sharper F = O(2)(+)O(7).) Therefore h^0(O(D_b)) = 2, and by (2.4), min_i a_i >= 2 and h^0(L_b) = 3, h^1(L_b) = 2, on **every** balanced geometric fibre.

This reproves working-context fact (WC-113) and discharges packet FND-0058 ("requires proof that h^0(omega_C(-D)) is constantly 3 on the whole balanced locus"). I do **not** assert the equivalence with excluding every non-primitive degree-four pencil: consistently with the recorded constraint, the argument excludes only the hyperelliptic-composed case, and covers factoring through a degree-two map onto a positive-genus intermediate curve retain h^0(D)=2 and are covered by the theorem with no change.

Now the base-change statement. Since min a_i >= 2 on every geometric fibre, h^1(P^1_b, E_b(-3)) = sum_i max(0,2-a_i) = 0. R^1 s_* is top-degree, hence commutes with arbitrary base change, so the geometric fibres of R^1 s_*(E(-3)) all vanish and R^1 s_*(E(-3)) = 0 by Nakayama. The splitting argument of Lemma 1.1 (perfect amplitude-[0,1] complex with vanishing H^1) then shows s_*(E(-3)) is locally free of rank 3 and commutes with arbitrary base change. For the other summand of (2.2), cohomology of O(m) on a relative projective line is computed by the standard Cech complex over any base, giving s_*O_P(-3) = 0 and R^1 s_*O_P(-3) locally free of rank 2 with arbitrary base change. Hence

  pi_*L = s_*(E(-3)) (x) T  locally free of rank 3, arbitrary base change;
  R^1 pi_*L = R^1 s_*O_P(-3) (x) T  locally free of rank 2, arbitrary base change.  (3.1)

**No reducedness of B is used.** This strictly widens the working-context fact restricted to reduced bases and supplies exactly the "separate scheme-theoretic constant-rank or lifting argument" that packet FND-0131 demands before pi_*L and R^1 pi_*L may be called vector bundles over every locally Noetherian base. It is not a constant-fibre-dimension argument, which would indeed be invalid over a nonreduced base (over k[eps] the module k has constant fibre dimension 1 and is not free).

## 4. The rank-drop scheme as an S_6-torsor over an open in a P^2-bundle (part D)

Let AJ := P_B(pi_*L) in the sub-line-bundle convention, i.e. AJ(T) = {invertible M on T together with a locally split injection M^{-1} -> (pi_*L)_T} modulo isomorphism. By (3.1) this is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle over B.

**Lemma 4.1.** AJ represents the functor Div_L: T -> {relative effective Cartier divisors G in C_T, flat of degree 6 over T, with O_{C_T}(G) = L_T (x) pi_T^*M for some invertible M on T}, modulo nothing (the pair (G) alone).

*Proof.* Given such a G, the canonical section 1 of O(G) transports under a chosen isomorphism to a section sigma of L_T (x) pi_T^*M; since G is a relative divisor it contains no fibre, so sigma_t is nonzero in H^0(L_t) for every t, and by (3.1) H^0(C_T, L_T (x) pi^*M) = H^0(T, (pi_*L) (x) M), so sigma is a map M^{-1} -> pi_*L_T which is nonzero in every fibre, hence a locally split injection (a nowhere-vanishing section of a bundle is a subbundle). Two choices of isomorphism differ by a unit in H^0(C_T, O^*) = H^0(T, O_T^*) because pi has geometrically connected fibres, so the resulting point of AJ is well defined. Conversely a locally split injection M^{-1} -> pi_*L_T gives, via (3.1), a section sigma of L_T (x) pi^*M nonzero on every fibre; its zero scheme is a relative effective Cartier divisor flat of degree 6, and the two constructions are mutually inverse. []

Let D_univ be the universal divisor on C_AJ and AJ^o the open locus of AJ over which D_univ -> AJ is etale (the etale locus of a finite flat morphism is open).

By CLM-0065-4 the T-points of Z are exactly the T-points (x_1,...,x_6) of Conf for which N_T = omega (x) W_5^vee(Gamma_T) = O(Gamma_T) (x) L_T^{-1} is of the form pi_T^*M_T, i.e. O(Gamma_T) = L_T (x) pi_T^*M_T. For such a point Gamma_T is the sum of six pairwise disjoint sections, hence finite etale of degree 6 over T. Therefore the assignment (x_1,...,x_6) -> Gamma_T is a morphism Z -> AJ^o by Lemma 4.1, and its fibre over a T-point of AJ^o is precisely the set of orderings of the degree-six finite etale T-scheme D_univ,T, i.e.

  Z = Isom_{AJ^o}( six constant copies of AJ^o , D_univ|_{AJ^o} ),  (4.1)

which is a finite etale S_6-torsor over AJ^o. Formation of both sides commutes with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change (Z by CLM-0065-4, AJ^o by (3.1) and Lemma 4.1). **No reduction is applied to either side**, which is the compatibility that packet FND-0087 requires and which the recorded constraint against "I_red -> I^{red-supp}" forbids violating; the torsor here is between two functorially defined, possibly nonreduced schemes.

## 5. Nonemptiness and density of the reduced-support open (part E)

This is the step that discharges the frontier obligation and packet FND-0083, and it is proved without any appeal to chi(L)=1 and without assuming L base-point-free. Fix a geometric point b over an algebraically closed field; write C = C_b, D = D_b, L = L_b = omega_C(-D), h^0(L) = 3 by Step 3, so |L| is a P^2.

**5.1 The fixed divisor.** By Riemann-Roch, h^0(L(-p)) = deg(L-p) - g + 1 + h^0(omega (x) L^{-1}(p)) = 0 + h^0(O_C(D+p)); so p is a base point of |L| iff h^0(O_C(D+p)) = 3 (this is (WC-118)). Suppose some p is a base point; then |D+p| is a g^2_5. Write |D+p| = B_0 + |M| with B_0 the base locus and |M| base-point-free of dimension 2 and degree 5 - deg B_0. The associated morphism phi_M: C -> P^2 is nondegenerate. If deg B_0 >= 1 then deg M <= 4: a birational image would be a plane curve of degree <= 4, of arithmetic genus <= 3 < 6, impossible; a non-birational one would map onto a nondegenerate plane curve of degree <= 2, i.e. a conic, making C a double cover of a rational curve, hence hyperelliptic, excluded by Step 3. So B_0 = 0 and |D+p| is a base-point-free g^2_5. If phi were non-birational of degree m > 1 onto its image, then m divides 5, so m = 5 and the image is a line - degenerate, excluded. Hence phi is birational onto a plane quintic, whose arithmetic genus 6 equals the geometric genus 6, so the image is smooth and phi is an isomorphism onto it. Thus C is a smooth plane quintic with hyperplane class H := O(D+p), omega_C = O_C(2H) by adjunction, D = H-p, and

  L = omega_C(-D) = 2H - (H-p) = H + p.

Since h^0(H+p) = 3 = h^0(H) (h^0(H+p) = 4 would give a g^3_6 with Clifford index 0, forcing C hyperelliptic), every section of L vanishes at p, so |L| = p + |H| and, |H| being very ample hence base-point-free, the fixed divisor of |L| is exactly the reduced point p. In particular no point occurs in the fixed divisor with multiplicity >= 2 (that would need h^0(L-2p) = 3, i.e. h^0(H-p) = 3, false since h^0(H-p) = 2).

Conclusion: the fixed divisor Fix of |L| is either 0 or a single reduced point, and in both cases |L| = Fix + |M| with |M| base-point-free of projective dimension 2. (Packet FND-0130 asserts that the plane-quintic tetragonal pencil is in fact unbalanced, so that on the balanced locus only the case Fix = 0 occurs; the argument above does **not** rely on that exclusion, and is therefore valid whichever way FND-0130 is resolved.)

**5.2 Characteristic-zero incidence count.** *Claim.* Let |M| be a base-point-free linear system of projective dimension r >= 1 on a smooth projective curve C over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Then the locus of non-reduced members is closed of dimension at most r-1 in |M| = P^r, and for any finite subset S of C the locus of members meeting S is a proper closed subset.

*Proof.* Base-point-freeness makes ev_x: H^0(M) -> M_x surjective for every x, so H_x := {s : mult_x div(s) >= 2} is a linear subspace of codimension 1 or 2 in H^0(M); codimension 1 holds exactly when every section vanishing at x vanishes to order >= 2 there, i.e. exactly when the morphism phi_M is ramified at x. In characteristic zero phi_M is separable and nonconstant (r >= 1), so its ramification locus R is finite. The incidence I = {(x,[s]) : mult_x div(s) >= 2} in C x P^r has fibre P(H_x) of dimension r-2 over x outside R and dimension r-1 over the finitely many x in R, so dim I <= max(1 + (r-2), 0 + (r-1)) = r-1 and its image, the non-reduced locus, has dimension <= r-1 < r. For the second statement, {s : s(x) = 0} is a hyperplane for each of the finitely many x in S. []

**5.3 Conclusion on the fibre.** Apply 5.2 with r = 2 and S = Supp(Fix). A member of |L| is Fix + (a member of |M|); it has six pairwise distinct support points iff the |M|-part is reduced and misses Supp(Fix), because Fix is reduced of degree <= 1. Hence the reduced-support locus of |L| = P^2 is a **nonempty dense open** whose complement is closed of dimension at most 1. The complement is also nonempty: for any p in C, evaluating a section and its first jet at p imposes at most two conditions on the 3-dimensional H^0(L), so h^0(L(-2p)) >= 1 and |L| contains a divisor non-reduced at p. So the reduced-support open is a nonempty proper dense open of the irreducible P^2, in particular not closed in the fibre - the two ingredients (a reduced member and a non-reduced member in the same fibre) that the recorded constraint requires before any non-closedness statement is made. I make this statement for the fibre only and assert nothing about closedness of any locus in M_{6,6}.

By Lemma 4.1 the fibre AJ^o_b is exactly this reduced-support open. Therefore AJ^o -> B is smooth (open in a P^2-bundle) with all geometric fibres nonempty of pure dimension 2, hence smooth and surjective of pure relative dimension 2; and by (4.1) Z -> AJ^o is finite etale and surjective (over an algebraically closed field a torsor under S_6 has 720 points over each point of the base), so

  Z -> B is smooth, surjective, of pure relative dimension 2, with nonempty geometric fibres.  (5.1)

This proves (E), and with it the frontier obligation "nonemptiness of the reduced-support open in |L_b| and of the ordered Conf_6 incidence on every balanced geometric fibre".

## 6. Ideal structure, regular immersion, and the excess bundle (part F)

P := Pic^0_{C/B} is an abelian scheme over B (rigidified by the first tautological section over Conf), smooth of relative dimension g = 6, and e is a section of a smooth morphism, hence a regular immersion of codimension 6 with locally free conormal I_e/I_e^2 of rank 6. Since Fit_0(coker phi) = a_N^*I_e is by definition generated by the pullbacks of local generators of I_e:

  **the rank-drop ideal is locally generated by exactly 6 elements**, and every irreducible component of Z has codimension at most 6 in Conf by Krull's height theorem.  (6.1)

This is a genuine computation of the ideal: a priori Fit_0 = I_12(phi) = I_6(phi_5) is generated by 462 maximal minors of an 11-by-6 matrix; (6.1) says six generators suffice locally, and identifies them.

By (5.1) Z is smooth over B of relative dimension 2 and Conf is smooth over B of relative dimension 6; a closed immersion of B-smooth schemes is a regular immersion, so Z -> Conf is a **regular closed immersion of relative codimension 4** with locally free conormal I_Z/I_Z^2 of rank 4. Note the logic: this is derived from proved smoothness of both schemes, not from the numerical comparison of expected codimension 6 with actual codimension 4, which the recorded constraints (and packet FND-0068) correctly forbid using for lci, regularity, purity or Gysin conclusions. Equally, I do not conclude non-lci from that comparison.

Since I_Z = a_N^*I_e . O_Conf, the induced map on conormals

  alpha: a_N^*(I_e/I_e^2)|_Z  ->>  I_Z/I_Z^2

is surjective from a rank-6 bundle onto a rank-4 bundle, so Exc := ker(alpha) is locally free of rank 2. Dualising 0 -> Exc -> a_N^*C_e|_Z -> C_Z -> 0 and splicing with the normal sequence 0 -> T_{Z/B} -> T_{Conf/B}|_Z -> N_{Z/Conf} -> 0 (exact on the left because both are B-smooth) identifies

  Exc^vee = coker( d a_N : T_{Conf/B}|_Z -> a_N^*T_{P/B}|_Z ).  (6.2)

This is the Fulton excess bundle in the form required by packet FND-0129 (the cokernel of d a_N, not its dual). Its value at a geometric point Gamma of Z is computed from 0 -> O_C -> O_C(Gamma) -> O_Gamma(Gamma) -> 0: the Abel-Jacobi differential is H^0(O_Gamma(Gamma)) = T_Gamma Conf -> H^1(O_C) = T_e Pic^0, with cokernel H^1(O_C(Gamma)) and kernel the image of H^0(O_C(Gamma)). On Z one has O(Gamma) = L up to pi^*, so

  rank(d a_N) = 6 - h^1(L) = 4,  dim ker(d a_N) = h^0(L) - 1 = 2,  Exc^vee at Gamma = H^1(C,L), dim 2.  (6.3)

The kernel computation independently reconfirms smoothness of Z of dimension 2: the Zariski tangent space of the scheme-theoretic fibre a_N^{-1}(e) at Gamma has dimension exactly 2, equal to dim_Gamma Z. So the excess of the generic determinantal expectation (codimension (11-5)(6-5) = 6 = g, the codimension of e) over the actual codimension 4 is not a numerical coincidence: it equals the corank of d a_N along Z, and the excess bundle is canonically the rank-two bundle R^1 pi_*L restricted to Z (up to the tautological twist). This answers, positively, the archived open question whether the numerical excess 2 has a genuine conormal/deformation-theoretic interpretation. Part (F) is proved.

## 7. The equation bundle (part G)

By CLM-0065-6 (confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109) there is an exact sequence on P

  0 -> End(F) -> p_*scriptW -> gamma_*W -> 0.  (7.1)

Under (H-BAL), End(F_b) = O (+) O (+) O(1) (+) O(-1) on every geometric fibre, so h^1 = 0 and h^0 = 4. Top-degree base change plus Nakayama give R^1 s_*End(F) = 0 (this is CLM-0065-8), and then the splitting argument of Lemma 1.1 makes s_*End(F) locally free of rank 4 commuting with arbitrary base change. Applying s_* to (7.1), using q_* = s_* o p_* and s_*gamma_*W = pi_*W:

  0 -> s_*End(F) -> q_*scriptW -> pi_*W -> R^1 s_*End(F) = 0.  (7.2)

Since pi_*W is locally free of rank 26 (CLM-0065-1), (7.2) is a short exact sequence of locally free sheaves and q_*scriptW is **locally free of rank 30**. For base change: pulling (7.2) back along any T -> B stays exact (pi_*W locally free kills Tor_1), and the natural comparison maps to the corresponding sequence formed over T are isomorphisms on the outer terms (both outer terms are pushforwards of bundles with vanishing R^1, and (H-CE), (H-BAL) are stable under base change), so the middle map is an isomorphism by the five lemma. Hence q_*scriptW commutes with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change.

Rank cross-check, independent of the Maroni type: h^0(P^1, Sym^2 E (x) F^vee) = 30 both for E = O(3)^3 and for E = O(2)(+)O(3)(+)O(4), as it must be, since 26+4 = 30.

Consequently the two ambient hypotheses carried by ATT-0065's theorem statement - the standard CE resolution, and finite local freeness with arbitrary base change of q_*scriptW - reduce on a balanced family to (H-CE) alone: the equation-bundle hypothesis is now proved, not assumed. This discharges the low-severity but explicitly open item FC-AMBIENT-EQN-BUNDLE-REMAINS-HYP raised in REV-0108 and the corresponding frontier obligation. Combining with CLM-0065-7 and CLM-0065-9, the ambient CE evaluation-failure scheme equals Z, with all of parts (D)-(F) applying to it.

## 8. Stack descent

Every construction above is canonical and commutes with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change: gamma_*, s_*, R^1 s_*, Fitting ideals, P_B(pi_*L), the etale locus of D_univ, and the Isom-scheme (4.1). Smoothness, relative dimension, surjectivity, regular immersion and local freeness are all smooth-local on the base. Hence for a locally Noetherian algebraic k-stack carrying the data, the statements hold on a smooth atlas, agree on the double overlap by canonicity, and descend by effective descent of quasi-coherent sheaves and ideals. This is the explicit descent remark that the recorded constraint (and packet FND-0127) requires before any scheme-level clause is quoted over the universal ordered configuration stack.

## 9. Constraints respected; blocked routes

None of the four blocked routes (vcd-only-vanishing, undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex, point-count-without-degree-parity-separation, forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown) appears anywhere in this argument; the artifact is purely geometric/determinantal and declares no new inputs. Constraints explicitly not walked: nonemptiness or reduced support is **not** inferred from chi(L)=1 (Step 5 is a fixed-part plus characteristic-zero incidence argument); the relative linear system is identified with P(pi_*L) only after h^0(L) = 3 is proved constant and after a scheme-theoretic base-change proof valid over nonreduced bases; no reduction is applied to one side only of the S_6-torsor; lci/regularity is derived from proved smoothness, never from the excess numbers 6-4 = 2 or h^1(L) = 2; no global splitting of F or of W is used; the equivalence of h^0-constancy with excluding all non-primitive pencils is not asserted; and no image, dimension, codimension, closedness, stabilizer, Gysin, purity, weight or Tate statement about M_{6,6} is made anywhere.

## 10. What is proved, assumed, and left open

**Proved here:** (A) the relative canonical normalisation from (H-CE); (B) the Maroni formulas (2.3)-(2.4); (C) constancy h^0(L) = 3 on the balanced locus together with local freeness and arbitrary base change of pi_*L and R^1 pi_*L over possibly nonreduced bases; (D) the exact torsor description (4.1) of the rank-drop scheme; (E) fibrewise nonemptiness and density of the reduced-support open and the resulting smooth surjection Z -> B of pure relative dimension 2; (F) six-generation of the rank-drop ideal, the codimension-4 regular immersion, and the rank-two excess bundle with its identification (6.2)-(6.3); (G) local freeness of rank 30 and base change for q_*scriptW.

**Source-backed inputs:** (H-CE), the degree-four CE structure theorem (SRC-0004 and the packet convention); the CE degree formula deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12-4f; working-context established facts (WC-112) and (WC-118); the verified dependency ATT-0065 with reviews REV-0108 and REV-0109.

**Computational hypothesis:** non-vacuity of (H-BAL), supported only by the pinned (1,2)-(2,2) example; not load-bearing.

**Left open (not claimed):** the image and closure of Z in M_{6,6} and its components, dimensions and stabilizers; whether Z^{bal} is closed; the unbalanced and non-reduced-support strata; full S_6 monodromy; every Hodge, weight, purity and Tate statement, including the exact target.

summary: Computes the balanced Casnati-Ekedahl determinantal rank-drop ideal and its fibre dimensions exactly, over an arbitrary (possibly nonreduced) locally Noetherian base. Six things are new. (1) The relative-canonical normalisation (N), listed as an external assumption on the frontier, is derived from the CE resolution alone by Koszul adjunction plus the Euler sequence, up to a harmless twist pulled back from the base. (2) A relative-duality computation gamma_*omega=(O(+)E)(-2) converts h^0(L) and h^1(L) into the Maroni splitting type of the Tschirnhausen bundle: h^0(L)=sum max(0,a_i-2). (3) That computation yields R^1 s_*(E(-3))=0 on the balanced locus, which upgrades local freeness and arbitrary base change of pi_*L and R^1 pi_*L from reduced bases (working-context fact; FND-0131 flags the gap) to all locally Noetherian bases, by a scheme-theoretic vanishing argument rather than a constant-fibre-rank argument. (4) The open frontier obligation of nonemptiness of the reduced-support open is settled: the fixed divisor of |L_b| is either zero or one reduced point (the plane-quintic case), and a characteristic-zero incidence count shows the non-reduced locus in |L_b|=P^2 is a proper closed subset of dimension at most one, so reduced members exist and are dense on every balanced geometric fibre. This is exactly what FND-0083 and the working-context constraints leave open, and it is proved without any appeal to chi(L)=1 and without assuming L base-point-free. (5) Combining with ATT-0065 (confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109), the rank-drop scheme Z in Conf_6(C/B) is canonically a finite etale S_6-torsor over a fibrewise-dense open of the P^2-bundle P(pi_*L) - with no reduction taken on either side, as FND-0087 requires - hence smooth and surjective over B of pure relative dimension 2, a regular immersion of relative codimension 4 whose excess bundle is canonically R^1 pi_*L of rank 2. (6) q_*scriptW is proved locally free of rank 30 with arbitrary base change, discharging the last standing ambient hypothesis of ATT-0065 flagged by REV-0108 (FC-AMBIENT-EQN-BUNDLE-REMAINS-HYP). Nothing is claimed about M_{6,6}.

theorem_scope.base: arbitrary locally Noetherian scheme over a characteristic-zero field, no reducedness or irreducibility hypothesis; all constructions commute with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change and descend along smooth atlases to algebraic stacks

theorem_statement: Let k be a field with char(k)=0 and let B be a locally Noetherian k-scheme. Let pi:C->B be smooth and proper with geometrically connected genus-6 fibres, let s:P:=P^1_B->B be the structure map and gamma:C->P finite flat of degree four with pi=s o gamma. In char 0 the trace splits gamma_*O_C=O_P (+) E^vee with E locally free of rank three; put X:=P_P(E^vee)->^p P in the convention p_*O_X(1)=E (so p_*O_X(2)=Sym^2 E), and q:=s o p. Assume: (H-CE) there is a closed P-immersion i:C->X whose ideal has the degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl resolution 0->O_X(-4) (x) p^*det F->O_X(-2) (x) p^*F->I_C->0 with F locally free of rank two on P; and (H-BAL) F_b is isomorphic to O(4)(+)O(5) on every geometric fibre of s. Put scriptW:=O_X(2) (x) p^*F^vee, W:=i^*scriptW, let 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 be the canonical filtration induced by the sub-line-bundle O_P(5) (x) s^*s_*F(-5) of F (ATT-0065, CLM-0065-5), and set O_C(D):=gamma^*O_P(1) and L:=W_5 (x) omega_{C/B}^{-1}, of relative degree 6. Let Conf:=Conf_6(C/B) be the open subscheme of the six-fold fibre product of C over B on which the six tautological sections are pairwise disjoint (smooth over B of relative dimension 6), Gamma their sum, phi:pi_*W->pi_*(W|_Gamma) the CE evaluation over Conf (locally free of ranks 26 and 12), N:=omega (x) W_5^vee(Gamma), a_N:Conf->Pic^0_{C/B} the classifying map, e the identity section, and Z:=V(Fit_0(coker phi)) the rank-drop scheme in Conf. Then: (A) det F is isomorphic to det E (x) s^*A for a unique invertible A on B, omega_{C/P} is isomorphic to O_X(1)|_C (x) pi^*A^{-1}, and consequently W_5 is isomorphic to omega_{C/B}^{(x)2}(-D) (x) pi^*T and L is isomorphic to omega_{C/B}(-D) (x) pi^*T for an invertible T on B; the relative-canonical normalisation is therefore a consequence of (H-CE), not an added hypothesis, and is canonical up to a twist pulled back from B. (B) gamma_*omega_{C/B} is isomorphic to (O_P (+) E)(-2) and gamma_*L to (O_P(-3) (+) E(-3)) (x) s^*T; hence on a geometric fibre with E_b isomorphic to the sum of O(a_i), a_1+a_2+a_3=9, one has h^0(L_b)=sum_i max(0,a_i-2), h^1(L_b)=2+sum_i max(0,2-a_i) and h^0(O_{C_b}(D_b))=2+sum_i max(0,2-a_i); in particular h^0(L_b)=3 if and only if min_i a_i>=2 if and only if h^0(O(D_b))=2. (C) (H-BAL) forces min_i a_i>=2 on every geometric fibre; hence R^1 s_*(E(-3))=0, pi_*L is locally free of rank 3, R^1 pi_*L is locally free of rank 2, and both commute with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change, with no reducedness hypothesis on B. (D) AJ:=P_B(pi_*L) is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle representing the functor of relative effective Cartier divisors of degree six in the class of L modulo pi^*Pic; if AJ^o is the open locus where the universal divisor is etale, then Z is canonically the Isom-scheme Isom_{AJ^o}(six copies of AJ^o, D_univ), a finite etale S_6-torsor over AJ^o, compatibly with arbitrary base change and with no reduction applied to either side. (E) On every geometric fibre b the fixed divisor of |L_b| (a P^2) is either zero or a single reduced point, AJ^o_b is a nonempty dense open of |L_b| whose closed complement is nonempty of dimension at most 1; consequently AJ^o->B and Z->B are smooth and surjective of pure relative dimension 2 with nonempty geometric fibres. (F) Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e is locally generated by six elements (the pullback of a regular sequence of length g=6), while Z->Conf is a regular closed immersion of relative codimension 4 with locally free conormal of rank 4; the excess bundle Exc:=ker(a_N^*(I_e/I_e^2)|_Z ->> I_Z/I_Z^2) is locally free of rank 2 with Exc^vee isomorphic to coker(d a_N)|_Z, and at each geometric point Exc^vee is H^1(C_b,O(Gamma))=H^1(C_b,L_b); thus the excess 6-4=2 of the generic determinantal expectation over the actual codimension is realised by the rank-two bundle R^1 pi_*L and not merely numerically. (G) q_*scriptW is locally free of rank 30 and commutes with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change, sitting in 0->s_*End(F)->q_*scriptW->pi_*W->0 with s_*End(F) locally free of rank 4; hence both ambient hypotheses of ATT-0065 hold automatically on a balanced family and the ambient CE rank-drop scheme equals Z. All statements descend along a smooth atlas to a locally Noetherian algebraic k-stack carrying the data. No assertion is made about images, closures, components, stabilizers, dimensions, monodromy, Gysin maps, weights, purity or Tate type in M_{6,6}.
